newsitem.title: UK: North Sea traders see rise in December loadings.
newsitem.headline: North Sea traders see rise in December loadings.

text.p: North Sea operators are set to announce bulging schedules for December loadings later this week, oil traders at equity holding companies said on Tuesday.
The traders said a maintenance-free month, the promise of rising production from newly-commissioned fields, and the 31-day month could add 5-10 cargoes to November's tally.
Britain's Forties and Brent systems are the best bet for larger liftings in December.
"They'll be two big fat programmes," said a trader.
Brent system volumes should be helped by rising production from the revamped Brent Charlie platform, brought back onstream in October.
Having suffered a hiccup on recommissioning after a six-month shutdown as part of the Brent system redevelopment Charlie in December should be on course for its peak 80,000 barrels a day (bpd).
Brent for November originally was expected to lift 42.2 cargoes, including the equivalent of four in top-ups, but an extra cargo was added this week.
Most traders were expecting two or three more in December. Some saw an outside chance of a lot more.
"It would be a brave man who'd put a five in front of a Brent programme this year but I'd say there's chance in December," said one North Sea trader.
Forties also was expected to better its 51-cargo count, including Grangemouth refinery volumes, for November.
Rising volumes from new Forties blend contributors, Thelma, Telford and Fergus, could push the system into the mid-fifties.
December's Flotta programme was announced on Wednesday at an unchanged 6.5 million barrels in 11 cargoes.
In Norway, traders said they saw no reason, weather permitting, for the five major export systems -- Statfjord, Gullfaks, Ekofisk and Oseberg -- not to repeat capacity volumes.
Outside the major systems, Britain's offshore-loading Beryl is due a boost from Mobil's Nevis while Shell's offshore-lifting Teal should be reaching peak 50,000 bpd capacity.
